note: Models run by run_benchmark.py when --models is not given (run=true). The unsloth/*-bnb-4bit repos are already 4-bit on Hugging Face (small download, no licence gate) and load as published. A normal repo id (e.g. Qwen/Qwen3-8B) also works: it downloads full weights and is quantized to 4-bit at load. VRAM/disk are approximate.

models.why: Baseline with no LLM: every rule-engine candidate accepted. Shows the recall ceiling and how much precision each model adds.
Strong, fast 7B; very reliable JSON output. Good small-model reference.
Newer Qwen generation; the pipeline turns thinking off (enable_thinking=False).
4-bit version of the model in your .env, so you have a before/after reference.
14B with strong reasoning for its size; MIT licence.
Best accuracy/speed balance in this list for a 32 GB GPU.
Widely used reference model; many medical fine-tunes are built on it.
Good multilingual (Bangla) ability; useful if notes are mixed-language.
Mid-size, fast for its size, strong instruction following.
Large Gemma; strong general medical knowledge.
Largest that fits 32 GB in 4-bit with room for context; likely accuracy ceiling of this list.
Gemma 4 small (4B effective). Newest Google generation; quantized to 4-bit at load.
Gemma 4 12B, quantization-aware trained for 4-bit, so it loses little accuracy at 4-bit.
Medical-domain Gemma (text only). The main medical model to compare against general models.
Biomedical fine-tune (quantized at load); weaker at strict JSON, worth one run for the medical-vs-general slide.
Medical reasoning model (quantized at load). Long thinking output can hit the token budget, so expect more JSON failures.
